sources.entry: ActivityWatch - Automatically track how you spend time on your devices. (Source Code) MPL-2.0 Python
ActivityWatch - Open-source automated time tracker that tracks how you spend time on your devices.

summary.one_liner: ActivityWatch is an open-source, local-first tool that automatically records which apps, window titles, browser tabs and AFK periods you spend time on, with the data kept under your control.
summary.what_it_does: The project is a meta-package bundling the core components and official modules of ActivityWatch as git submodules, and publishes full-suite releases. The server (aw-server in Python, or aw-server-rust) stores timestamped events in buckets and exposes a REST API with buckets, events, heartbeat and query endpoints. Watchers feed it data: aw-watcher-window records the active application and window title, aw-watcher-afk detects away-from-keyboard status from keyboard and mouse input, and aw-watcher-web tracks website time. The web UI (aw-webui) offers dashboards, timelines, a query explorer, a raw data browser and JSON export. Client libraries (aw-client for Python, aw-client-js, aw-client-rust) support writing custom watchers. Sync is described as work in progress and decentralized.
use_cases: automatically track time spent on apps and websites
find out where my working hours actually go
measure time spent coding in editors
write a custom watcher to collect more personal activity data
keep time-tracking data private on my own machine
export activity data as JSON for analysis
how_to_run: Download a release from the releases page
Follow the getting-started guide in the ActivityWatch documentation
To build from source, see the building guide in the documentation
notable: Local-first data storage: events are kept on the user's machine with a REST API for querying
Modular watcher architecture: window, AFK, browser and editor watchers, plus support for custom watchers
Two server implementations: Python default and a Rust version planned as the future default
Citable via Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4957165, with a BibTeX entry in the README
caveats: The README lists iOS as unsupported; supported platforms are Windows, macOS, Linux and Android per the comparison table
Sync is marked as work in progress in the README
Installation details are delegated to external documentation; the README itself gives no step-by-step install commands
keywords: track how i spend my time
